title: Vector Akhmediev Breathers and State Transitions in the Degenerate and Nondegenerate Regimes for the Coupled Sasa-Satsuma System
authors: Mengyuan Lan, Lei Wang, Yinchuan Zhao
abstract: We investigate vector Akhmediev breathers (ABs) in the degenerate and nondegenerate regimes for the coupled Sasa-Satsuma system describing two coupled ultrashort optical pulse envelopes. Based on the carrier-wavenumber relations of the two-component background, we examine three configurations: a single vanishing wavenumber, a pair of opposite wavenumbers, and two nonzero wavenumbers of unequal magnitudes. These configurations admit distinct maximal degrees of nondegeneracy. For each configuration, we derive the reduced spectral equations, construct the existence diagrams, and compare the resulting branches with the modulation-instability gain spectra. Owing to the distinct carrier-wavenumber symmetries, nondegenerate-type modes can occur in spectrally degenerate regions, whereas degenerate-type ones may also appear in spectrally nondegenerate regions. Moreover, all admissible branches in the degenerate regimes satisfy the state-transition condition and correspond to periodic-wave states, while such branches are also present in nondegenerate regimes. Direct numerical simulations of representative solutions further confirm the analytical predictions.
summary: This paper analyzes vector Akhmediev breathers in the coupled Sasa-Satsuma system, a model for coupled optical pulses. By comparing the spectral analysis of breathers with the linear modulation instability spectrum, the authors establish a deep link: the condition for zero linear gain precisely corresponds to the state-transition condition for the breathers. This unifies the understanding of stable and unstable wave states in this nonlinear system.
main_problem: The paper investigates the existence and properties of vector Akhmediev breathers (ABs) and the associated state transitions within the coupled Sasa-Satsuma (CSS) system.
main_result: The analysis establishes a direct correspondence between admissible characteristic-root pairs derived from the spectral analysis and the linear Modulation Instability (MI) branches, showing that zero-gain MI corresponds to periodic-wave states.
method: The study employs spectral analysis using Lax pairs, Darboux transformations to construct breathers, and linear stability analysis to determine the MI gain spectrum.
model_or_system: The governing equation is the coupled Sasa-Satsuma (CSS) system, which models the coupled propagation of two ultrashort optical pulse envelopes. The analysis is performed across three distinct carrier-wavenumber configurations.
key_observables: Vector Akhmediev Breathers (ABs), MI gain $G(\chi_a; \gamma)$, and the localization variable $\Psi$.
important_parameters: Carrier wavenumbers ($ eta_1,  eta_2$), spectral parameters ($\lambda$), and the degeneracy/nondegeneracy of the background state.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes specific configurations for the background carrier wavenumbers and relies on the equivalence between MI conditions and characteristic-root equations.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the existence diagram in the $( eta_2, \gamma)$ plane for the case $ eta_1 = 0$, distinguishing between degenerate and nondegenerate regimes.
paper_structure: The paper follows a structure moving from spectral analysis (defining the background), to classifying AB branches based on wavenumber configurations, then analyzing the linear modulation instability (MI) spectrum, and finally establishing the correspondence between the two.
why_interesting: The connection drawn between the state-transition condition (from breathers) and the zero-gain condition (from MI) provides a powerful unified diagnostic tool for understanding nonlinear wave dynamics in optical systems.

Dashed vertical and horizontal lines indicate common values of β2 and γ, respectively.

FIG. 2. Branch-resolved MI gain in the (β2, γ) plane for β1 = 0, with c1 = c2 = 1 and α = 0. The three panels correspond to the eigenvalue-branch pairs represented by χ1, χ3, and χ5, respectively. Nonzero gain identifies AB-supporting branches, while “ST” denotes admissible branches satisfying the state-transition condition and reducing to periodic-wave states. The annotated coordinate points A3 = (4, 0.7) and A4 = (2, 0.7) are used in the representative analyses below, with the dashed horizontal line indicating their common γ = 0.7.

FIG. 3. State-transition periodic waves in the degenerate regime for β1 = 0, corresponding to points A1 and A2 in Fig. 1. (a) Region III at A1 = (−4, 8.2), with χa = χ3 = −4.1 −0.1366i and χb = 4.1 −0.1366i. (b) Region III′ at A2 = (−4, 2.1), with χa = χ3 = −1.0500 −0.8309i and χb = 1.0500 −0.8309i. In both cases, Re(χa) = −γ/2, with χ4 forming the other member of the unique admissible eigenvalue-branch pair. The intensity modulations are synchronous in region III and opposite in region III′. For each case, the upper row shows |u1|2, |u2|2, and |u1|2 + |u2|2 from left to right, and the lower row gives the corresponding t = 0 cross sections.
